title: First day at work
intro:
On your first day you will very likely be asked to introduce yourself to your team, often at a morning meeting ({朝礼[ちょうれい]}) or as you are walked around the office. Prepare a short speech of about 30 seconds to a minute. A common structure is:

- Your name, with the department you are joining: {本日[ほんじつ]から〜でお世話[せわ]になります}.
- Where you are from and what you did before.
- One light personal detail, if you like.
- A humble closing, asking for guidance: {ご指導[しどう]よろしくお願[ねが]いいたします}.

You will also handle paperwork: the employment contract, social insurance enrollment, a bank account for salary, your commuting route for the commuting allowance, and your My Number, which employers need for tax and social insurance. Read the work rules ({就業[しゅうぎょう]規則[きそく]}) for working hours, leave and overtime.

Learn the daily phrases. Say {おはようございます} when you arrive, {お疲[つか]れ様[さま]です} when you pass colleagues during the day, {お先[さき]に失礼[しつれい]します} when you leave before others, and {お疲[つか]れ様[さま]でした} to people who are leaving. Ask questions freely in the first weeks; it is expected of a newcomer. You will probably be assigned a mentor or senior colleague ({先輩[せんぱい]}) to help you.

Take notes, learn names and roles quickly, and watch how colleagues behave. Every workplace has its own unwritten rules.

phrases.jp: 本日[ほんじつ]から営業部[えいぎょうぶ]でお世話[せわ]になります、スミスと申[もう]します。
phrases.en: I'm Smith, and I'm joining the sales department from today.

phrases.jp: 前職[ぜんしょく]ではITサポートを担当[たんとう]しておりました。
phrases.en: In my previous job I worked in IT support.

phrases.jp: 一日[いちにち]も早[はや]く仕事[しごと]を覚[おぼ]えられるよう、頑張[がんば]ります。
phrases.en: I'll do my best to learn the job as quickly as possible.

phrases.jp: 至[いた]らない点[てん]も多[おお]いかと思[おも]いますが、ご指導[しどう]よろしくお願[ねが]いいたします。
phrases.en: I'm sure I have a lot to learn, so I would appreciate your guidance.
phrases.note: A classic humble closing for a work self-introduction.

phrases.jp: 何[なに]かお手伝[てつだ]いできることはありますか。
phrases.en: Is there anything I can help with?

phrases.jp: すみません、これはどうすればよろしいでしょうか。
phrases.en: Excuse me, what should I do with this?

phrases.jp: メモを取[と]ってもよろしいですか。
念[ねん]のため、確認[かくにん]させてください。
phrases.en: Just to be sure, let me confirm.

phrases.jp: 教[おし]えていただき、ありがとうございます。
お手洗[てあら]いはどちらですか。
〜さんは、どちらの部署[ぶしょ]ですか。
お昼[ひる]、ご一緒[いっしょ]してもいいですか。
phrases.en: May I join you for lunch?

phrases.jp: お疲[つか]れ様[さま]です。
phrases.en: (greeting / thanks to colleagues during the day)

phrases.jp: お先[さき]に失礼[しつれい]します。
phrases.en: Excuse me for leaving before you.

phrases.jp: お疲[つか]れ様[さま]でした。
phrases.en: Thanks for your hard work. (to someone leaving)

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.jp: 皆[みな]さん、おはようございます。今日[きょう]から新[あたら]しいメンバーが入[はい]りました。スミスさん、一言[ひとこと]お願[ねが]いします。
dialogue.en: Good morning, everyone. A new member joins us from today. Mr. Smith, a few words, please.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: はい。本日[ほんじつ]から開発部[かいはつぶ]でお世話[せわ]になります、ダニエル・スミスと申[もう]します。
dialogue.en: Yes. I'm Daniel Smith, and I'm joining the development department from today.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: アメリカ出身[しゅっしん]で、前職[ぜんしょく]ではアプリの開発[かいはつ]をしておりました。
dialogue.en: I'm from the US, and in my previous job I developed apps.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: 日本語[にほんご]はまだ勉強[べんきょう]中[ちゅう]で、ご迷惑[めいわく]をおかけすることもあるかと思[おも]いますが、一日[いちにち]も早[はや]くお役[やく]に立[た]てるよう頑張[がんば]ります。
dialogue.en: I'm still studying Japanese, so I may cause you some trouble, but I'll work hard to be useful as soon as possible.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: どうぞよろしくお願[ねが]いいたします。
dialogue.en: I look forward to working with you all.

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.jp: ありがとう。じゃあ、田中[たなか]さん、スミスさんの指導[しどう]係[がかり]をお願[ねが]いできるかな。
dialogue.en: Thanks. Ms. Tanaka, could you be Mr. Smith's mentor?

dialogue.speaker: Tanaka
dialogue.jp: はい。スミスさん、田中[たなか]です。わからないことがあったら、何[なん]でも聞[き]いてくださいね。
dialogue.en: Sure. Mr. Smith, I'm Tanaka. If there's anything you don't understand, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: ありがとうございます。よろしくお願[ねが]いします。
dialogue.en: Thank you. I look forward to working with you.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: お先[さき]に失礼[しつれい]します。

dialogue.speaker: Tanaka
dialogue.jp: お疲[つか]れ様[さま]でした。また明日[あした]。
dialogue.en: Thanks for today. See you tomorrow.

tips: Rehearse your self-introduction out loud until you can say it without notes. Keep it short.
Say {お疲[つか]れ様[さま]です} to superiors, not {ご苦労[くろう]様[さま]です}, which is traditionally used toward people of lower rank.
Your employer will ask for your My Number. Giving it to your employer is normal and required for tax and social insurance.
Bring a notebook and write things down. Asking the same question twice is fine; asking it five times is less so.
Watch what time people actually arrive and how they leave. Workplace culture varies a lot between companies, especially between traditional Japanese firms and foreign-owned ones.
